Focused extraction fixture

Reliable conversion begins by keeping the source article separate from page chrome, transient controls, and promotional content. Reviewers need a stable representation that can be inspected before a markdown export is compressed or summarized.

When an article contains concrete headings, explanatory prose, code samples, and links, the extraction stage should retain those structures without relying on the browser tab after capture. That makes a stored capture useful for deterministic reprocessing and regression tests.

Fixture-driven validation records the smallest example that demonstrates a behavior. It lets a future change distinguish an extraction regression from a parser regression or a markdown rendering regression, rather than presenting a single ambiguous export failure.

Local processing also keeps the review path private. A developer can reproduce the output, compare the source with the focused article, and measure changes without sending page content or diagnostic output to another service.
